description: MODIS/CAMS aerosol optical depth — an independent satellite aerosol signal (unitless).
interpretation: Aerosol Optical Depth — a unitless satellite measure of how much aerosol the atmospheric column holds. An independent signal (not a ground reading); higher = hazier.
label: Haze from satellite (AOD)

description: Coarse (~40 km) CAMS regional PM2.5 the local model sits on — the atmospheric context term.
interpretation: Coarse (~40 km) regional-model background PM2.5 — the atmospheric context the local surface builds on. Smooth by design; the modelled surface adds the local detail this can't resolve.
label: PM2.5 regional background (CAMS)

description: Detected pollution hotspot clusters (tiered Info/Warning/Critical) where PM2.5 breaches CPCB thresholds.
interpretation: Clusters of adjoining cells that breach PM2.5 thresholds, tiered Info / Warning / Critical. Most useful when pollution is localised (a few bad pockets); when the whole area is uniformly severe the city reads as one large cluster.
label: Pollution hotspots

description: Hyperlocal per-H3-cell PM2.5 surface — ML feature-model nowcast where available (else IDW of station readings).
interpretation: Hyperlocal modelled PM2.5 (µg/m³) for every ~500 m H3 cell. Where reference monitors exist the surface is anchored to them; elsewhere a machine-learning model estimates concentrations from atmospheric background, weather, land-use and traffic proxies. Colours follow AQI bands (green = Good … maroon = Severe). Use the time scrubber to compare hours or seasons.
label: PM2.5 now (estimated from stations)

description: building footprint coverage (Google Open Buildings)
interpretation: Building footprint area/coverage per cell — the built density under the air surface.
label: Building coverage

description: Individual building footprints (Google Open Buildings v3), extruded on cell drill-in.
interpretation: Individual building footprints, extruded in 3D by height. Drill a cell to inspect.
label: Building outlines (3D)

description: share of cell that is built
interpretation: Fraction of each cell that is built-up (impervious). A proxy for density + local emissions.
label: Built-up area

description: Official Census of India 2011 ward population ÷ ward area (BBMP 198 wards; DataMeet / Open Bangalore). Each cell carries its ward's figure.
interpretation: The whole ward is one colour (darker blue = denser). Official counts, but 2011 — the outer wards have grown a lot since. Compare with the GHSL 2020 'Population density' layer, a 100 m model that can over-allocate commercial cores.
label: Population density: census 2011 (wards)

description: How many shortest travel-time routes on the arterial network pass through the cell (sampled betweenness, OpenStreetMap).
interpretation: A PROXY for where congestion concentrates — not observed traffic. Darker red (and taller in 3D) = the city's routes depend more on this stretch.
label: Chokepoints (network proxy)

description: Critical facilities (schools, hospitals, police/fire, govt, utilities) from OpenStreetMap — points overlay + cell drill-in.
interpretation: Critical facilities (hospitals, schools…) as points — who is exposed where.
label: Facilities (count per cell)

description: Predicted ponding risk per cell (0–1) from terrain, drainage and a rainfall scenario — a prediction, not an observation.
interpretation: Predicted ponding risk for the rainfall scenario the engine ran (0–1). Darker red (and taller in 3D) = higher risk. Shown only once this city has risk.flood records.
label: Flood risk

description: height above nearest drainage (MERIT Hydro)
interpretation: Flood susceptibility per cell from terrain + drainage (HAND). Higher = more prone to waterlogging.
label: Flood susceptibility

description: vegetation share of cell
interpretation: Fraction of each cell under vegetation. Correlate with heat + PM2.5 (greener = usually cooler/cleaner).
label: Green cover

description: mean surface temperature
interpretation: Mean surface temperature per cell — read alongside built-up + green cover to spot urban heat islands.
label: Heat: land surface temperature

description: Share of each cell that was open water, per year, over the city's lakes — JRC Global Surface Water (Landsat, 30 m), 1995–2021, one method throughout. Press play to watch lakes shrink or refill.
interpretation: Darker blue = more of the cell was water that year. Weeds, hyacinth or algae on the water read as land, and desilting or a dry year as loss (Bellandur 2019–21 was weed-clearing / desilting).
label: Lakes: water extent 1995–2021

description: Night-time light radiance per year from NASA/NOAA VIIRS (yearly median of the monthly composites), 2014–2025 — press play to watch the city light up. A satellite proxy for economic and energy activity.
interpretation: Darker blue (and taller in 3D) = brighter at night that year. A PROXY for activity: commercial areas, roads and industry glow most, so it is not a measure of household income.
label: Night lights 2014–2025

description: Estimated resident population density per H3 cell, from GHS-POP (JRC GHSL).
interpretation: A 2020 MODEL (JRC GHSL, 100 m): people spread by built-up volume, so dense commercial cores can be over-allocated (e.g. one Cottonpete cell at ~198,000 /km², 1.7x the densest census ward). The colour scale stops at the city's 99th percentile so one spike does not wash out the rest. Cross-check with 'Population density — census 2011 (by ward)'.
label: Population density: 2020 model

description: Hourly precipitation forecast per cell (Open-Meteo). Temporal — use the time scrubber to animate.
interpretation: 48-hour rainfall forecast per cell — scrub time to animate the forecast.
label: Rain forecast: next 48 h

description: Mean annual rainfall per H3 cell — a multi-year climatological normal from ERA5 (Open-Meteo archive).
interpretation: Annual-normal rainfall per cell (climatology, not live).
label: Rainfall: annual normal

description: road length per km² (OpenStreetMap)
interpretation: Road length/density per cell — a traffic-emission proxy; correlate with the PM2.5 surface.
label: Road density

description: All built properties from the GIS property survey — the cadastral base the tax gap is measured against.
interpretation: The full universe of surveyed built properties. Those NOT lit up as unregistered are the ones the engine matched to a tax-register record.
label: Surveyed properties (cadastre)

description: Surveyed built properties with NO matching record in the property-tax register — candidates for field verification.
interpretation: Each point is a property the GIS survey found but the tax register does not carry. Confidence reflects how many independent signals fired (unregistered footprint, utility with no tax, satellite new-build).
label: Unregistered properties (tax gap)

description: Number of BBMP tenders whose title names the cell's ward.
interpretation: Each cell carries its WARD's tender count. Tenders whose title names no ward are not on the map.
label: Tenders by ward

description: elevation (m above sea level)
interpretation: Elevation / slope per cell — the physical relief the city sits on.
label: Terrain (elevation)

description: People living beyond a walkable bus stop (> 500 m) or metro station (> 1 km), weighted by population (OpenStreetMap stops).
interpretation: Darker red (and taller in 3D) = more people far from a bus stop or metro station. Straight-line distance, not walking route; OSM stop coverage may be incomplete.
label: Transit access gap

description: How walkable the street grid is: junction density, street density and few dead ends (OpenStreetMap), as city percentiles.
interpretation: Darker green (and taller in 3D) = a finer, better-connected street grid. Based on street layout only — not footpath quality, safety or shade.
label: Walkability

description: Net amount paid on BBMP public works in the cell's ward — cumulative over the works register (work orders 2013–2021 mostly; OpenCity BBMP). Press play to see it year by year (by work-order year, 2012–2022).
interpretation: Each cell carries its WARD's figure — the whole ward is one colour. Static view = all years together; the time slider steps through work-order years (a work's payments are counted in the year it was ordered; the register's payments carry no dates).
label: Works spend by ward 2012–2022
